summary: CCC-erected lookout on Dutch Creek Mountain, built 1933 and removed 1972; a 2010 Forest Service decision covers a communications site at the summit.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a small, glass-enclosed lookout house on top
facts.status_note: Lookout removed in 1972; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the summit

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps erected a lookout structure
Lookout record gives 1972 as the removal year
Forest Service decision signed 11/05/2010 extending Entergy's special-use authorization for communication facilities at the Dutch Creek Mountain Tower site

evidence.supports: Lookout built in 1933 by the Civilian Conservation Corps
evidence.quote: 1933: A lookout structure erected by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: Station and tower on the summit of Dutch Creek Mountain
evidence.quote: THE SUMMIT OF DUTCH CREEK MOUNTAIN

evidence.supports: Tower design: four-legged steel structure with a glass-enclosed lookout house
evidence.quote: THE TOWER IS A 4-LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE WITH A SMALL, METAL, GLASS-ENCLOSED, LOOKOUT HOUSE ON TOP.

evidence.supports: Overall height about 71 feet (68 feet to eaves plus estimated 3-foot gable)
evidence.quote: THE HEIGHT OF THE STRUCTURE IS 68 FEET TO THE EAVES WITH THE GABLE BEING ESTIMATED AT 3 FEET, MAKING AN APPROXIMATE OVERALL HEIGHT OF 71 FEET.

evidence.supports: Survey description tied to a 1956 station recovery
evidence.quote: RECOVERY NOTE BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1956 (LSB)

evidence.supports: Forest Service project titled as the Dutch Creek Mountain Tower, Entergy special-use extension
evidence.quote: Dutch Creek Mountain Tower - Entergy Special Use Extension

evidence.supports: Forest Service extended Entergy's special-use authorization for communication facilities
evidence.quote: Extend special use authorization for Entergy Corporation for operation of communitcation facilities

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'unknown' corrected to removed (1972). The 1933 build and 1972 removal come from one hobbyist page that reproduces NGS text; no agency or register page for those dates was found. The 2010 Forest Service record is the only current-site source and does not mention whether any lookout structure remains. Brief height 21.6 m matches the 71 ft overall height in the NGS text. No staffing or fire records found. A photo or site check would firm up the 'what remains' answer. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the facts.access block ('restricted') was removed because no source found supports an access level or describes public access to the summit.
